proposals.title: Anchor causal video answers to the actual visible interaction
proposals.trigger: Before each native decision in this task, using only current public observations and earlier public feedback.
procedure: Read the question and options, then examine the ordered sequence at the event that distinguishes the options. Identify state before contact, the contact itself and the resulting state.

For what-caused questions distinguish the acting entity from any separate implement. Track whether a distinct object is actually interposed at the contact; do not infer a conventional implement from the usual way this event is done.

A barely visible or absent object must not be invented to make a familiar story. Prefer direct evidence of the interaction to canonical expectations; however lack of one sampled frame alone does not prove absence.
For temporal direction or order use early, intermediate and late states in the supplied order, including reversal. For counts, count distinct completed events, not repeated frames of one event.

Use prerequisite temporal/evidence modules only where their public event model fits. The already supplied frames cannot be supplemented with imaginary tools. Select the supported option in the exact native response format.
successSignals: Native objective achieved; actual feedback agrees with the selected action.
failureSignals: Action repeats a known failure or depends on an unverified observation or model.
recovery: Re-read the actual public feedback, identify whether perception, model or execution was wrong, and revise only that assumption.
invariants: No fixed object names, choices or case-specific events in the skill.
Causal plausibility cannot override visible event evidence.
